### LOW: Candidate\-controlled script output is appended to GITHUB\_ENV before the version is validated
[\.github/workflows/provider\-signing\-validation\.yml:64](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/46e10b98108043c669a334cbc97b434e5113dbf2/.github/workflows/provider-signing-validation.yml#L64) · T-034, T-054

The new build\-job step runs \`candidate/scripts/provider\_release\_identity\.py "$EXPECTED\_VERSION"\` from the source\_sha checkout and appends its raw stdout to \`$GITHUB\_ENV\`\. It runs before \`check\-release\-version\.sh\` validates the version\. The checkout only needs a verified signature, not review\. A candidate script, or a version input containing newlines, can therefore set arbitrary variables for every later step\. Examples are BASH\_ENV, PATH, DYLD\_INSERT\_LIBRARIES and SDKROOT\. Those later steps include \`tooling/scripts/provider\-signing\-validation\.py stage\`, which is meant to be trusted tooling, and the metallib fetch\. The unsigned tarball that the signing job later signs with the Developer ID certificate is produced there\. Because candidate Package\.swift and build scripts already execute in this job, the extra exposure is modest\. The signing job has the same shape with trusted tooling: the script's stdout is written to GITHUB\_ENV in a job that later receives signing secrets, and the \`version\` dispatch input is passed to it without prior validation\. Fix: have the workflow parse the output against an allowlist of exact keys \(APP\_NAME, CLI\_NAME, ENCLAVE\_NAME, PRODUCT\_\*, DARKBLOOM\_RELEASE\_ENVIRONMENT\)\. Reject values with newlines or unexpected characters, validate \`version\` with a strict regex first, and take the identity from the trusted \`tooling\` checkout in both jobs\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### MEDIUM: Dev and prod apps share one bundle ID, signing identity and keychain group, so side\-by\-side installs share hardware\-bound credentials
[\.github/workflows/release\-swift\.yml:15](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/46e10b98108043c669a334cbc97b434e5113dbf2/.github/workflows/release-swift.yml#L15) · A-002, A-015, T-055, T-058

The header comment states that dev releases install beside production while the bundle identifier and signing identity stay identical\. The Info\.plist step keeps CFBundleIdentifier=io\.darkbloom\.provider, and the same provisioning profile and keychain\-access\-group are embedded\. Dev apps are published on every master push without a tag\. On one Mac, a dev build can therefore load the production persistent SE key \(label io\.darkbloom\.provider\.attestation\-signing\.v2\) and the same\-app\-ID App Attest credential\. This lets a dev\-channel binary sign attestation or challenges for the production identity\. The same SE public key is also visible to both the dev and prod coordinators, which links the two environments' sessions\. Existing controls such as binary\-hash and CodeDirectory qualification and the per\-connection process X25519 key limit the damage\. Even so, this weakens the dev/prod credential separation that T\-055 and T\-058 assume\. Fix: give the dev app a distinct bundle ID, keychain label or access group \(and profile\), or document and test that dev builds cannot use production credentials\. Update the threat model either way\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Dev/prod cache isolation claim relies on keychain label prefixes while the signed access group stays shared
[docs/architecture/security/encryption\.md:108](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/46e10b98108043c669a334cbc97b434e5113dbf2/docs/architecture/security/encryption.md#L108) · A-002, A-003, T-041

The new text says a dev build has its own KEK and Secure Enclave key \(prefix \`io\.darkbloom\.dev\`\), 'so it cannot read a production provider's cache, and the reverse'\. The release workflow still asserts and signs the single team\-scoped keychain access group \`SLDQ2GJ6TL\.io\.darkbloom\.provider\` for the CLI \(lines 638\-649\)\. Dev and prod binaries are signed with the same Developer ID and the same APNs identity, and the changelog calls the shared APNs identity a 'documented limitation'\. So separation is by item label only, not by an access\-group or cryptographic boundary\. A dev build with a label or prefix bug, or a compromised or less\-reviewed dev build, could read or delete the production KEK and Secure Enclave key and so reach production encrypted KV\-cache artifacts\. This is a plausible weakening of the T\-041 'KEK wipe / unreadable cache' assumption\. Fix: soften the wording to 'separate by label, not enforced by the OS'\. Better, give dev builds a distinct keychain access group \(and entitlement check\) or a distinct signing identity, and add the shared APNs identity and shared access group to the threat model\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### MEDIUM: Dev and prod installs share the Hugging Face weight cache, so a lower\-assurance dev build can feed production serving
[docs/operations/provider\-release\.md:274](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/46e10b98108043c669a334cbc97b434e5113dbf2/docs/operations/provider-release.md#L274) · A-004, T-012, T-027

The new section says the HF hub cache is shared on purpose\. A dev install without its own ref reuses production's \`refs/main\` selection, and \`models remove\` in one install deletes weights for the other\. The dev build talks to the dev coordinator, is unreleased and is less trusted\. If it downloads, repairs or re\-pins a revision into the shared cache, the production provider can load those bytes, because weight\-hash enforcement is fail\-open \(SEC\-007\)\. Consumers would then get output from substituted weights \(T\-012, T\-027\)\. Removal in either install also lets one install disrupt the other's availability\. Fix: give dev its own hub cache or snapshot namespace, or make production verify weight hashes and refuse revisions that dev wrote\. Update the threat model to cover the cross\-install cache as an A\-004 tamper surface\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### MEDIUM: Documented APNs topic collision lets a dev process receive production code\-identity challenges
[docs/operations/provider\-release\.md:286](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/46e10b98108043c669a334cbc97b434e5113dbf2/docs/operations/provider-release.md#L286) · T-034, T-042, T-057, TB-009

The doc admits both installs share bundle ID \`io\.darkbloom\.provider\`, so they get the same APNs topic and device token\. A production code\-identity challenge can be delivered to the dev process, and apsd delivers each push to only one process\. This is a new coexistence condition, flagged as pending test\. Impact: the production provider may miss or fail challenges, accumulate strikes and lose or drop its CodeAttested legacy trust \(availability, T\-057\-like\)\. A dev\-built binary with a different hash and key also now sits on the production push path \(T\-042, T\-034\)\. The doc also calls dev and prod on one Mac supported while the fix, a separate dev bundle ID or profile, is not done\. Fix: gate the side\-by\-side feature on that change, or have the provider reject or ignore pushes whose challenge is not bound to its own key, and say so in the threat model\. TB\-009 and T\-042 need a note on shared APNs delivery\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Shared root fan helper now holds per\-session leases from two installs; threat model does not cover the new lease semantics
[docs/operations/provider\-release\.md:258](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/46e10b98108043c669a334cbc97b434e5113dbf2/docs/operations/provider-release.md#L258) · A-014, T-044, T-046, T-047, TB-010

Both installs use one root LaunchDaemon \(\`io\.darkbloom\.fan\-helper\`\)\. The doc describes helper v2 per\-session leases, \`fan disable\` and \`fan uninstall\` that affect both installs, and an older v1 helper whose single Mac\-wide lease is owned by whichever provider renewed last\. A hung or stale dev provider can hold a live lease and keep fans in manual mode \(T\-047\), or deny another install's restoration to Auto \(T\-046\)\. A pre\-change provider has no helper version check\. Whether lease isolation prevents one install from renewing or releasing another's lease depends on code not in this diff\. TB\-010 and T\-044/T\-047 still describe a single provider lease and should be updated, and the lease\-per\-session bounds verified\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### MEDIUM: Dev and prod installs share an APNs topic, so code\-identity challenges can reach the wrong process
[docs/operations/provider\-release\.md:285](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/46e10b98108043c669a334cbc97b434e5113dbf2/docs/operations/provider-release.md#L285) · T-034, T-042, T-057, TB-009

The documented side\-by\-side dev and prod installs use the same bundle ID, \`io\.darkbloom\.provider\`, so they register one push topic and one device token\. The doc says a production code\-identity challenge can reach the dev process on the legacy path without App Attest\. The challenge is encrypted to the production provider's key, so the dev process cannot answer it\. The production provider can then miss challenges and be marked untrusted or unroutable, or a dev build can interfere with prod attestation\. The T\-034/T\-042 challenge design and T\-057 availability analysis assume that one device token maps to one provider process\. The PR documents this as a known limitation but does not add it to the threat model\. Fix: add this cross\-delivery case to the T\-034/T\-042/T\-057 analysis, or use a separate dev bundle ID and provisioning profile\. Until then, forbid co\-installation of dev and prod on providers that serve production traffic\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Fan helper shared across installs; older helper or provider has weaker per\-session lease isolation
[docs/operations/provider\-release\.md:258](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/46e10b98108043c669a334cbc97b434e5113dbf2/docs/operations/provider-release.md#L258) · A-014, T-044, T-047, TB-010

A single root fan helper, \`io\.darkbloom\.fan\-helper\`, now serves both dev and prod providers\. Helper version 2 keeps one lease per provider session\. The doc says a version 1 helper keeps one lease for the whole Mac, so the last provider to renew owns it\. It also says a provider built before this change lacks the check that stops it replacing a newer helper with an older one\. A stale or older provider could therefore downgrade the root helper to the single\-lease semantics\. A dev build could also shorten or extend the fan policy of a production provider\. This touches the T\-044, T\-046 and T\-047 assumptions about lease ownership and stale authority, and the threat model does not cover it\. Fix: record the shared\-helper and downgrade case in TB\-010/T\-047\. The helper should refuse older\-provider replacement on the root side, not rely on provider\-side checks\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

findings.detail: The new `identity` step in the build job runs `provider_release_identity.py --source candidate`, which reads the identity file from the candidate commit. Its output is written to both `$GITHUB_ENV` and `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`. The signing job (`needs.build.outputs.*`) then uses APP_NAME, CLI_NAME and ENCLAVE_NAME to build filesystem paths and codesign targets, for example `$RUNNER_TEMP/signing-stage/$APP_NAME` and `$app/Contents/MacOS/$CLI_NAME`. The signing job also writes the decoded provisioning profile into `$app/Contents/`. This runs while the Developer ID certificate, profile and notarization credentials are loaded. The names were previously hard-coded. The step guarantees only that the verified commit signature check passed, not that the source was reviewed. The visible workflow does not show validation of these values for path separators, `..` or newlines before they reach `$GITHUB_ENV` and the signing steps. If `provider_release_identity.py` accepts such values, a candidate source file could redirect the profile write or the signing and verification targets outside the stage directory, or inject extra environment variables. The `unpack` check compares the app against the build-produced `unsigned-files.json`, which comes from the same candidate-influenced values, so it adds no independent check. Fix: have the script enforce strict allow-list patterns (single path component, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`, no newlines). Alternatively re-derive or re-validate the names in the signing job from trusted tooling rather than from build outputs.
findings.title: Signing job uses candidate-derived names for paths and codesign targets without visible validation
